method:
Mechanical enumeration of the IRIS features each module's code uses (gate 3.2-coverage), classified against the
IRIS environment contract.

pure.premise: P2-PURE: ObjectScript and SQL value built-ins compute their documented value inside the calling process and touch no shared state
pure.consequence: no transaction, lock, visibility, durability or concurrency result depends on them; value-level statements (key and name encodings, parsing, numeric canonical forms, string building) rest on the documented semantics and on the module's own live and run evidence on this engine, not on the contract

sqlexpr.premise: P2-SQLEXPR: SQL scalar and aggregate functions, predicates, joins, grouping, ordering and subqueries compute their documented answer over the rows the statement reads (which rows it reads, and what it locks, is the contract's: E-VIS, E-ROWLOCK, X-NOINDEX)
sqlexpr.consequence: query answers of readers and the filters of writers (e.g. COALESCE graph guards are X-NULL; %EXACT and %SQLUPPER collation of string comparisons, %STARTSWITH, %INLIST, LIKE are not) rest on the documented semantics; no contract result changes, but a reader result that depends on collation or on a function's edge case is evidenced only by the module's live/run tests

plan.premise: P2-PLAN: plan hints (named %IGNOREINDEX, %PARALLEL, %FIRSTTABLE, %NOFLATTEN, %PROFILE, ...) change the plan only, not the rows a statement reads or writes (the documented exception, %NOINDEX rows, is X-NOINDEX)
plan.consequence: readers that force a plan (EdgeScan's %IGNOREINDEX on labels/props, eraser scans) are assumed to read the same rows as without the hint; X-NOINDEX shows a by-key statement on a key with a %NOINDEX duplicate may reach different rows by plan, so that combination stays outside

clock.premise: P2-CLOCK: clocks advance and are not used to order events between processes
clock.consequence: time windows (lock timeouts in seconds, HANG, minimum-age purges, cache windows such as the strict-mode 5 s window HD-0801, timestamps in receipts) are untimed in every model and in the contract (wait/no-wait only); a result that depends on elapsed time holds only as observed on this container

random.premise: P2-RANDOM: $RANDOM and generated GUIDs are arbitrary values
random.consequence: values drawn from them are treated as arbitrary; no result depends on their distribution or uniqueness beyond what the product checks itself

hash.premise: P2-HASH: $SYSTEM.Encryption digests, encodings and $ZCRC compute their documented functions
hash.consequence: receipts' and digests' equality checks compare outputs of the same function; their value as a commitment is assumed

status.premise: P2-STATUS: an error inside a method reaches its caller as a %Status or exception whose text carries the cause (SQLCODE, error name); %Status handling is ObjectScript language semantics
status.consequence: how product errors surface in Python and are classified (by text or SQLCODE) is evidenced by the modules' live tests and by E-1 (env2-e1-r1: a %Status from AssertTemporalRow carried SQLCODE -108 to the Native API caller), not by a clause; the r6 note that a DB-API error carries the connection's last ObjectScript error (env/explore-8) applies

dict.premise: P2-DICT: the pin's classes are compiled as the pin's own deploy path leaves them, and run-time dispatch by name ($CLASSMETHOD, $PROPERTY, %Dictionary reads) reaches them
dict.consequence: deploy, upgrade and introspection results (modules 01, 17, 18) rest on the compiled state observed in the audit's namespaces; run-time compilation ($SYSTEM.OBJ, objectgenerator code) is out of the audit's scope and is evidenced only by the product's own suites (validation lane)

sqlroutine.premise: P2-SQLROUTINE: a compiled SQL routine ([SqlProc], CREATE FUNCTION/PROCEDURE, CALL) runs its ObjectScript in the calling connection's server process and transaction
sqlroutine.consequence: SQL-callable entry points other than Txn_Begin/End/Undo (validated as S-1 when env2-e1-r2 passes) are assumed to behave as their ObjectScript body called from that process

epy.premise: P2-EPY: embedded Python methods run in the calling IRIS process, sharing its transaction and locks
epy.consequence: embedded Python is not driven by the contract (it needs irispython in the container); results of modules whose writers run as embedded Python rest on the premise

job.premise: P2-JOB: a JOB or WorkMgr worker is a separate server process with its own transactions and locks, started outside the caller's transaction
job.consequence: parallel builds and algorithms (modules 04, 09, 10) are modelled, where at all, as independent writers; WorkMgr queueing, worker reuse, error propagation and the caller's waiting are not modelled; a caller's rollback does not undo a worker's writes (assumed)

temp.premise: P2-TEMP: IRISTEMP globals (^IRIS.Temp*, ^CacheTemp*, ^mtemp) are not journaled, not undone by a rollback, lost at restart and shared by every process of the instance
temp.consequence: scratch state kept there is treated as non-durable and non-transactional; any reasoning that a rollback or a crash restores it would be wrong; not testable within the audit's scratch-global rule (^IVGAudit*)

sysglobal.premise: P2-SYSGLOBAL: system globals and structured system variables (^$LOCK, ^$GLOBAL, ^%..., ^ROUTINE, ^rINDEX) report the engine's current state
sysglobal.consequence: introspection results (lock-table reads, routine and index inventories) are observations of this engine only

ns.premise: P2-NS: namespaces have the default mappings: ^KG, ^NKG, ^IVG.* and the IVG schema's tables live in the namespace's own database; switching namespace changes only the default database
ns.consequence: every result is per namespace; a site with package or global mappings (e.g. ^KG mapped to a shared database) is not covered

security.premise: P2-SEC: the caller has the privileges the product needs (the audit runs as _SYSTEM)
security.consequence: results do not cover least-privilege callers except where the validation lane ran one; web dispatch (%CSP.REST), roles and SQL privileges are not modelled

mgmt.premise: P2-MGMT: management APIs (%SYS.ProcessQuery, %SYSTEM.Process other than Terminate, %SYSTEM.Version, console log, %SYSTEM.Util) report the engine's state and act as documented
mgmt.consequence: process enumeration, version checks and logging by the product are observed live only; process stop is E-STOP

task.premise: P2-TASK: Task Manager tasks run in their own process at their schedule
task.consequence: scheduled work (modules 06, 15) is not modelled; its writes are those of an independent writer

stream.premise: P2-STREAM: stream data is stored in globals written in the caller's transaction like any global
stream.consequence: stream columns and properties (docs, snapshots, ledger payloads if any) are assumed to roll back with the transaction; not validated

file.premise: P2-FILE: files and devices are outside transactions and journaling: a rollback does not undo a file write, and file I/O is not observed by the journal oracle
file.consequence: snapshot files (module 18, F-C1803) and any export/load through files are covered only by the module's live tests; no rollback or crash result covers file contents

device.premise: P2-DEVICE: output to the principal device in a method called through the Native API is not part of the call's result
device.consequence: diagnostic WRITEs do not affect any result

zf.premise: P2-ZF: $ZF callouts run native code in the calling process
zf.consequence: results that depend on the Arno callout (module 10, F-1001) are outside the contract; the x86_64 library is unavailable here

vecop.premise: P2-VECOP: $VECTOROP computes its documented element-wise and aggregate operations
vecop.consequence: vector math in ObjectScript (similarity, normalisation) rests on the documentation; $VECTOR set/get and rollback is X-VEC

hnsw.premise: P2-HNSW: an HNSW index is maintained by the row's statement and answers approximate nearest neighbours
hnsw.consequence: vector-search answers (modules 06, 17, 18) and their recall are observations only; HNSW maintenance in transactions and build effects are not modelled

ifind.premise: P2-IFIND: iFind tokenisation, the word dictionary and ranking behave as documented (only the per-row entries' transaction behaviour is X-FX)
ifind.consequence: full-text search answers (modules 01, 03, 06, 07, 08) rest on the tokenizer and ranking; the word dictionary is written outside the transaction (a rolled-back word stays in the dictionary but finds no row)

embedding.premise: P2-EMBEDDING: EMBEDDING() and %Embedding configurations compute vectors as configured
embedding.consequence: embedding generation (module 06) is not modelled; vectors are opaque values

absent.premise: absent on IRIS 2026.1 Community (%AI classes, InterSystems FHIR server storage)
absent.consequence: every result that depends on these classes is blocked-access (versions/AVAILABILITY.md)

fk.premise: P2-FK: foreign keys refuse a child row without its parent (-121) and a parent delete with children (-124); under concurrency the check's visibility and locking are as documented (the parent row is checked with a shared lock unless %NOLOCK)
fk.consequence: the product's FK-based guards (rdf_edges -> nodes, labels/props/embeddings -> nodes; AssertTemporalRow's -121 retry) rest on the premise; E-1 observed -121 only as a code the product maps, not its concurrency

trigger.premise: P2-TRIGGER: triggers and object callbacks run in the row's statement and transaction
trigger.consequence: trigger-maintained state (system %OBJJRN*/%OBJGUID triggers on DDL tables; any product trigger) is assumed to roll back with the row

persistent.premise: P2-OBJ: object filing (%Save, %OpenId, %DeleteId, %ExistsId, %KillExtent, %BuildIndices) writes the same rows, indexes and locks as the equivalent SQL
persistent.consequence: results about persistent classes (ledger revision classes in module 11, FHIR/registry classes in 15, snapshot bookkeeping in 18) rest on this; object concurrency modes are not modelled

iou.premise: P2-IOU (residual after X2-IOU): INSERT OR UPDATE of a key whose row another open transaction deleted, and upserts on keys with several rows, behave as documented
iou.consequence: X2-IOU (env2-x2-r1) shows an upsert waits for a row another transaction holds and fails with SQLCODE -109 when that transaction rolls back an insert of the key; upserts in modules 06, 15, 18 can therefore surface -109 under a concurrent rolled-back writer; the deleted-key case is outside

top.premise: P2-TOP (residual after X2-TOP): TOP / LIMIT over keys equal under SQLUPPER (case variants), over %NOINDEX duplicates, or ordered by expressions other than a column, behave as documented
top.consequence: X2-TOP (env2-x2-r1) decides TOP n / LIMIT n [OFFSET m] over ORDER BY a VARCHAR column (SQLUPPER string order: 1, 10, 2, ...; not numeric), DESC and %EXACT; paged and 'first row' readers rest on the residual only for the forms listed

ddl-other.premise: P2-DDL: DDL forms other than CREATE/DROP TABLE and ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN (CREATE/DROP INDEX, CREATE VIEW, other ALTER TABLE forms, TRUNCATE) take effect at once and are undone by a rollback that covers them, as X-DDL is
ddl-other.consequence: schema-migration results (modules 01, 17) for those forms rest on the analogy with X-DDL

catalog.premise: P2-CATALOG: catalog views other than INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES / COLUMNS, %Dictionary through SQL and default-schema resolution answer the current definitions
catalog.consequence: introspection (schema detection, route discovery, version probes) is observed only

isolation.premise: P2-ISO: SQL isolation-level / commit-mode settings other than the default are not used at run time
isolation.consequence: if a caller sets READ COMMITTED or %COMMITMODE, the contract's E-VIS and E-AUTOCOMMIT do not apply

lock-esc.premise: P2-ESC: lock escalation: a process holding more than the threshold (default 1,000) row locks on one table in one transaction takes a table lock; #"E" names the escalating lock type
lock-esc.consequence: bulk transactions over one table (EraseGraph / EraseAll deletes, bulk loads in a caller's transaction) can block every other writer of that table, of every graph; the structural lane observes it live (structural/capkeys/cap_batch.py case 03); the contract treats #"E" as exclusive and models no escalation

lock-local.premise: P2-LOCKNAME: lock names without a caret and indirect lock names are lock-table entries with the same semantics as global names (E-LOCK-*)
lock-local.consequence: lock plans that use them are read as E-LOCK-* plans; not exercised by the contract's cases

query.premise: P2-QUERY (residual after X2-QUERY): $NAME and $QUERY over references with quoted or very long subscripts behave as documented
query.consequence: walkers that build names with $NAME (eraser roots, snapshot export) rest on the residual

merge.premise: P2-MERGE (residual after X2-MERGE): MERGE between overlapping subtrees and MERGE with local variables behave as documented
merge.consequence: X2-MERGE (env2-x2-r1) decides MERGE copy / onto existing / rollback and ZKILL value-only / rollback

seq.premise: P2-SEQ: $SEQUENCE allocates values unique across processes, increasing per process, in ranges, not undone by a rollback (observed in env2-x2-explore, not validated)
seq.consequence: id allocation with $SEQUENCE is assumed unique; the global's stored value can run ahead of the values returned, so readers of the global must not treat it as a count

list.premise: P2-LIST (residual after X2-LIST): $LISTVALID, $LISTUPDATE, SET $LIST(...), non-canonical numeric literals ($LB(1.0) is encoded as 10E-1), exponents and non-ASCII string elements behave as documented
list.consequence: list-encoded keys, payloads and snapshot records rest on the residual for those forms; X2-LIST (env2-x2-r1) decides the read functions and the driver's IRISList decode

buildindices.premise: P2-BUILDIDX: %BuildIndices / %PurgeIndices (also with parallel jobs, whose workers are WorkMgr processes) rebuild the named indexes from the rows outside the caller's transaction, as BUILD INDEX does (X-NOINDEX), and leave other connections' cached code consistent
buildindices.consequence: BuildKG's parallel adjacency rebuild (TraversalBuild.cls:129-133), schema rebuilds and the P-1715 <LIST ERROR> after another connection's %BuildIndices (utils.py:114-130) rest on it; X-NOINDEX shows BUILD INDEX is outside the caller's transaction and needs the extent lock

limits.premise: P2-LIMITS: engine limits (long strings up to 3,641,144 characters, subscript length, bound-parameter count, $ZF heap) are not reached by the module's inputs
limits.consequence: inputs near a limit (large property values, long ids, wide IN lists, big snapshot lines) fail with <MAXSTRING>, <SUBSCRIPT> or a parameter-count error; the module's live tests cover only the sizes they used; capacity lanes (structural/capkeys) observe some limits live

oracle.premise: P2-JOURNAL: the IRIS journal records every global write of a journaled database with its process and transaction markers (the audit's oracle, traces/journal.py; not a contract clause)
oracle.consequence: journal-oracled results (footprints, trace conformance, env2-e1-r1-journal) rest on the journal's completeness; non-journaled writes (IRISTEMP, %NOJOURN) are invisible to it

sqlparse.premise: P2-SQLTEXT: the SQL text the module builds (comments, multi-statement text, literal escaping, identifier quoting) is parsed by IRIS as the module intends
sqlparse.consequence: generated SQL (Cypher translation, module 08) is evidenced by the product's suites and TCK runs, not by the contract

bitmap.premise: P2-EXTENT: the bitmap extent and index-driven full-table DML reach every row the statement names (env/explore-4 A11: DELETE without WHERE misses %NOINDEX rows)
bitmap.consequence: full-table deletes over tables loaded with %NOINDEX (bulk loads before their rebuild) can leave rows

subscript.premise: P2-NATIVESUB: the Native API validates subscripts as ObjectScript does (null subscripts refused)
subscript.consequence: Native API walks and writes with empty-string subscripts (snapshot import/export, module 18) rest on it

fetchfirst.premise: P2-FETCH: FETCH FIRST / OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT is not used against this engine
fetchfirst.consequence: on IRIS 2026.1 Community with the locked driver 5.3.2 every FETCH FIRST form probed (with and without ORDER BY, FETCH FIRST 0, OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT) killed the Python client process with SIGSEGV while TOP and LIMIT answered (env2-fetchfirst-probe); the product runs its FETCH FIRST probe in a subprocess and falls back to TOP on a crash (engine.py:726-840), so query results use TOP; any FETCH FIRST path that bypasses the probe would crash the client

json.premise: P2-JSON: the %DynamicObject / %DynamicArray members and forms not exercised by env2-x2-r1 (%GetIterator, %Size, %Push, JSON literal constructors with content, a %Library.DynamicObject-typed column, SQL JSON functions) behave as documented
json.consequence: JSON payloads (ledger changesets, qualifiers, reports) rest on the documentation; the product's prefix test on serialised qualifiers ('{"temporal":true', Adjacency.cls:661) depends on %ToJSON's output form

indirection.premise: P2-INDIR: name indirection (@) and XECUTE resolve to the same references as the literal text
indirection.consequence: writers through indirection (RetractTemporalRows' @pRoot@, eraser roots, generic loaders) are attributed by the writer census's resolution, not by the contract

rowid.premise: P2-ROWID: row ids (%ID, IDENTITY, IDKEY) are unique, stable while the row exists, and allocated outside the transaction (the journal shows the id counter SET outside the transaction, env2-e1-r1-journal)
rowid.consequence: lookups and deletes by %ID (RetractTemporalRow) and id-based paging rest on it; ids are not reused after a rollback (gaps)

batch.premise: P2-BATCH (residual after X2-BATCH): executemany over keys another process holds behaves per row as execute does
batch.consequence: X2-BATCH (env2-x2-r1) confirms the product's premise (_batch_check.py:1-4): a refused row of several is skipped without an error and rowcount counts the written rows; one refused row raises

irislist.premise: P2-IRISLIST (residual after X2-LIST): the driver's getIRISList / classMethodIRISList paths decode as IRISList(bytes) does
irislist.consequence: X2-LIST (env2-x2-r1) decides IRISList over bytes read by getBytes; other driver entry points are assumed equal

sqlcode.premise: P2-SQLCODE: SQLCODEs other than the contract's observed ones (-30, -104, -108, -110, -119, -201, -359, -400) are reported for the documented conditions
sqlcode.consequence: the product's error mapping for these codes (e.g. -121 FK, -124, -114/-110 lock timeouts, -1/-12 syntax, -29/-30 names, -99 privilege, -149 function errors, -428/-461 etc.) is evidenced only by their own tests; a misclassification would change an error surface, not stored data

config.premise: P2-CFG: the deployment configuration (cpf merge files, compose files, install scripts) yields an instance equivalent to the audit container
config.consequence: results hold for the audit container's configuration (IRIS 2026.1 Community defaults, SynchCommit=0); settings the deploy files change (licences, services, memory, journal settings) are not covered

esql-other.premise: P2-ESQL: embedded SQL forms not exercised by E-1 (cursor FETCH loops over many rows, embedded UPDATE, embedded statements with %INLIST / %STARTSWITH / named %IGNOREINDEX) behave as their dynamic forms
esql-other.consequence: E-1 (env2-e1-r1) validated embedded SELECT INTO, a DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH cursor read, INSERT, INSERT ... SELECT WHERE NOT EXISTS and DELETE against the contract; other embedded forms rest on the same premise by analogy

web.premise: P2-WEB: web dispatch (%CSP.REST, &js/&html) serves requests in a CSP server process
web.consequence: REST and web surfaces (modules 07, 09, 16) are observed through their HTTP behaviour only

language.premise: P2-LANG: ObjectScript language features (dynamic dispatch on objects, %New, object references, Try/Catch) behave as documented
language.consequence: no environment result depends on them
